title: Gulab Jamun

description: Gulab Jamun are soft, melt-in-your-mouth fried dough balls traditionally made from milk solids and soaked in a fragrant sugar syrup. This classic Pakistani dessert is a staple at celebrations and special occasions, offering a delightful sweet finish to any meal.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sugar Syrup
instructions.text: In a saucepan, combine sugar, water, and crushed cardamom pods. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Reduce heat and simmer for 5-7 minutes until slightly thickened, but not a string consistency. Remove from heat, stir in rose water, and keep warm.

instructions.title: Mix Dry Ingredients for Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together milk powder, all-purpose flour, and baking powder until well combined. Ensure there are no lumps.

instructions.title: Form the Dough
instructions.text: Add melted ghee or butter to the dry ingredients and mix with your fingertips until crumbly. Gradually add milk, one tablespoon at a time, and gently bring the mixture together to form a soft, smooth dough. Do not over-knead, as this can make the jamuns hard. The dough should be slightly sticky but manageable.

instructions.title: Shape the Gulab Jamuns
instructions.text: Divide the dough into 16-20 equal portions. Gently roll each portion between your palms to form smooth, crack-free balls. Ensure there are no cracks on the surface, as they can break during frying. Keep them covered to prevent drying.

instructions.title: Fry the Gulab Jamuns
instructions.text: Heat oil or ghee in a deep frying pan over very low heat. The oil should be warm, not hot. Carefully add the shaped jamuns to the oil, making sure not to overcrowd the pan. Fry them on very low heat, gently turning them occasionally, until they are evenly golden brown all over. This slow frying ensures they cook through and absorb the syrup well. This will take about 10-15 minutes.

instructions.title: Soak in Syrup
instructions.text: Once the gulab jamuns are golden brown, remove them from the oil using a slotted spoon and immediately transfer them to the warm sugar syrup. Let them soak in the syrup for at least 30 minutes, or preferably for a few hours, to allow them to absorb the syrup and become soft and juicy.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Serve the Gulab Jamuns warm or at room temperature, garnished with chopped pistachios. These delightful sweets are perfect for any festive occasion or as a comforting dessert.

tips: Always fry Gulab Jamuns on very low heat. If the oil is too hot, they will brown quickly on the outside but remain raw inside.
Ensure your dough balls are smooth and crack-free before frying. Any cracks will cause them to break apart in the hot oil.
For best results, let the Gulab Jamuns soak in the warm syrup for several hours or even overnight. This allows them to become incredibly soft and absorb maximum flavor.
